source.text: דִּבְרֵ֤י׀אָג֥וּר בִּן־יָקֶ֗ה הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א נְאֻ֣ם הַ֭גֶּבֶר לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: The words of Agur son of Jakeh, the oracle; the utterance of the man to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal.

en.L: The words of Agur son of Jakeh, the oracle. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
en.B: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh, an oracle. This man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
en.R: These are the words of Agur, the son of Jakeh. This is his message. He spoke it to Ithiel and to Ucal:

fr.L: Les paroles d’Agur, fils de Jaké, l’oracle. Cet homme déclare à Ithiel, à Ithiel et à Ucal :
fr.B: Paroles d’Agur, fils de Jaké, un oracle. Cet homme déclare à Ithiel, à Ithiel et à Ucal :
fr.R: Voici les paroles d’Agur, fils de Jaké. Voici son message. Il l’a adressé à Ithiel et à Ucal :

sw.L: Maneno ya Aguri mwana wa Yake, ujumbe mzito. Mtu huyo anamwambia Ithieli, Ithieli na Ukali:
sw.B: Maneno ya Aguri mwana wa Yake, ujumbe mzito. Mtu huyu anamtangazia Ithieli, Ithieli na Ukali:
sw.R: Haya ni maneno ya Aguri, mwana wa Yake. Huu ndio ujumbe wake. Aliwaambia Ithieli na Ukali:

decisions.choice: the oracle: a weighty message
decisions.reason: The word (massa) is a "burden," the term for a prophet's solemn message (Isaiah 13:1; Malachi 1:1). It may instead be a name: Massa was a son of Ishmael and the people descended from him in north Arabia (Genesis 25:14). Then Agur, and perhaps Lemuel (31:1), were from Massa.

decisions.choice: the man declares: a formal opening of a solemn utterance
decisions.reason: The phrase (neum haggever) introduces the sayings of Balaam (Numbers 24:3, 15) and David's last words (2 Samuel 23:1).

decisions.choice: to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal: two names, as the Hebrew vowels read
alternatives: I am weary, O God, I am weary, O God, and worn out
There is no God; there is no God, and I can prevail
decisions.reason: The vowels added to the text read two personal names, the people Agur speaks to. The same letters, divided differently, can be read as a cry: "I am weary, O God, I am weary, O God, and I am spent." That reading fits the humble confession of verses 2–3. Another division reads a skeptic's claim that Agur goes on to answer. The meaning is very uncertain.

decisions.choice: "Agur, fils de Jaké", "Ithiel", "Ucal"
decisions.reason: Agur follows the terms note. The other names have no settled French form in common use; they are transcribed from the Hebrew as the English does, with the French "é" for the final vowel of Jakeh.

decisions.choice: "Aguri mwana wa Yake", "Ithieli" and "Ukali" for the names
decisions.reason: The names take the usual Swahili shape, ending in a vowel. "Yake" is spelled like the word for "his", but as a name after "mwana wa" and with its capital it reads as a name.

source.text: כִּ֤י בַ֣עַר אָנֹכִ֣י מֵאִ֑ישׁ וְלֹֽא־בִינַ֖ת אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely I [am] more stupid than anyone, and the understanding of a person [is] not mine.

en.L: Surely I [am] more brutish than anyone, \q and I do not have [the] understanding of a human.
en.B: I am surely the most ignorant of all people; \q I lack ordinary human understanding.
en.R: I am more ignorant than anyone else. \q I do not have the understanding that people should have.

fr.L: Certes, je [suis] plus stupide que quiconque, \q et je n’ai pas l’intelligence d’un homme.
fr.B: Je suis vraiment le plus ignorant de tous ; \q il me manque l’intelligence ordinaire des humains.
fr.R: Je suis plus ignorant que tous les autres. \q Je n’ai pas l’intelligence que les gens devraient avoir.

sw.L: Hakika mimi [ni] mjinga kuliko mtu yeyote, \q wala sina ufahamu wa mwanadamu.
sw.B: Hakika mimi ndiye mjinga kuliko watu wote; \q sina ufahamu wa kawaida wa mwanadamu.
sw.R: Mimi ni mjinga kuliko mtu mwingine yeyote. \q Sina ufahamu ambao watu wanapaswa kuwa nao.

decisions.choice: stupid: dull as an animal
decisions.reason: The word (baar) is used of a person no wiser than a beast (12:1; Psalm 73:22). Agur confesses that human wisdom cannot reach God (verses 3–4); the confession is humble, perhaps with some irony.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־לָמַ֥דְתִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים אֵדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have not learned wisdom, and knowledge of [the] Holy One I know.

en.L: I have not learned wisdom, \q nor do I know [the] knowledge of [the] Holy One.
en.B: I have not learned wisdom, \q nor do I have knowledge of the Holy One.
en.R: I have not learned wisdom. \q I do not know the Holy God.

fr.L: Je n’ai pas appris la sagesse, \q et je ne possède pas la connaissance du Saint.
fr.B: Je n’ai pas appris la sagesse, \q et je n’ai pas la connaissance du Saint.
fr.R: Je n’ai pas appris la sagesse. \q Je ne connais pas le Dieu saint.

sw.L: Sijajifunza hekima, \q wala sijui maarifa ya Aliye Mtakatifu.
sw.B: Sijajifunza hekima, \q wala sina maarifa ya Aliye Mtakatifu.
sw.R: Sijajifunza hekima. \q Simjui Mungu Mtakatifu.

decisions.choice: nor do I know the knowledge of the Holy One
alternatives: yet I have knowledge of the Holy One
decisions.reason: The negative of the first line carries over to the second. Without it, the line would mean that Agur does know God, in contrast to his lack of learning.

decisions.choice: the Holy One: God
decisions.reason: The plural (qedoshim) is a plural of majesty for God, as in 9:10.

source.text: מִ֤י עָלָֽה־שָׁמַ֨יִם׀וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף־ר֨וּחַ׀בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר־מַ֨יִם׀בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ מַה־שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה־שֶּׁם־בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Who has gone up [to] heaven and come down? Who has gathered [the] wind in the hollow of his hands? Who has wrapped [the] waters in a cloak? Who has set up all [the] ends of [the] earth? What [is] his name, and what [is] the name of his son? Surely you know!

en.L: Who has gone up [to] heaven and come down? Who has gathered [the] wind in the hollow of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands? Who has wrapped [the] waters in a garment? \q Who has set up all [the] ends of [the] earth? \q What [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, and what [is] the name of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} son? Surely you know!
en.B: Who has climbed up to heaven and come back down? Who has caught the wind in the palms of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands? Who has bundled the waters in a cloak? \q Who has fixed all the boundaries of the earth? \q What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, and the name of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} son? Tell me, if you know!
en.R: Has anyone gone up to heaven and come back? Who can hold the wind in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands? Who can wrap up the oceans in a coat? \q Who made the edges of the world? \q What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name? What is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} son's name? Tell me if you know!

fr.L: Qui est monté [aux] cieux et en est descendu ? Qui a recueilli le vent dans le creux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains ? Qui a enveloppé les eaux dans un vêtement ? \q Qui a établi toutes les extrémités de la terre ? \q Quel [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, et quel [est] le nom de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} fils ? Certainement, tu le sais !
fr.B: Qui est monté au ciel et en est redescendu ? Qui a saisi le vent dans le creux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains ? Qui a serré les eaux dans un manteau ? \q Qui a fixé toutes les limites de la terre ? \q Quel est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, et le nom de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} fils ? Dis-le-moi, si tu le sais !
fr.R: Quelqu’un est-il monté au ciel et en est-il revenu ? Qui peut tenir le vent dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains ? Qui peut envelopper les océans dans un manteau ? \q Qui a fait les bords du monde ? \q Quel est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom ? Quel est le nom de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} fils ? Dis-le-moi, si tu le sais !

sw.L: Ni nani aliyepanda [mbinguni] na kushuka? Ni nani aliyekusanya upepo katika viganja vya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}? Ni nani aliyefunga maji katika vazi? \q Ni nani aliyeweka miisho yote ya dunia? \q Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} [ni] nani, na jina la mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [ni] nani? Hakika unajua!
sw.B: Ni nani aliyepanda mpaka mbinguni na kushuka tena? Ni nani aliyeukamata upepo katika viganja vya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}? Ni nani aliyeyafunga maji katika joho? \q Ni nani aliyeiweka mipaka yote ya dunia? \q Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni nani, na jina la mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}? Niambie, kama unajua!
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu aliyepanda mbinguni na kurudi? Ni nani awezaye kushika upepo mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}? Ni nani awezaye kufunga bahari katika koti? \q Ni nani aliyefanya miisho ya dunia? \q Jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni nani? Jina la mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ni nani? Niambie kama unajua!

decisions.choice: who has done these things: only God
decisions.reason: The questions are like those God asks Job (Job 38:4–11). No human has gone up to heaven to learn its secrets; only the Creator holds wind and water and fixed the earth's ends. The answer to "What is his name?" is God.

decisions.choice: the name of his son
alternatives: God's people Israel, called his son
a son who could reveal God
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament Israel is called God's son (Exodus 4:22; Hosea 11:1), and the king is called his son (Psalm 2:7). The question may ask who could know God as a son knows his father. Christian readers have also heard in it a pointer to the Son who came down from heaven (John 3:13).

decisions.choice: surely you know: a challenge to the hearer
decisions.reason: The words echo God's challenge to Job (Job 38:5), with a note of irony: no one can answer.

decisions.choice: Tell me, if you know!
decisions.reason: The challenge is put as a direct question, so the irony is plain.

decisions.choice: "Certainement, tu le sais !" at Literal; "Dis-le-moi, si tu le sais !" at Balanced and Readable
alternatives: "Tu le sais sûrement !" at every level
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the Hebrew's challenge as it stands, the other levels say it as a French challenge would be said (meaning decision m3).

source.text: כָּל־אִמְרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Every word of God [is] refined; a shield he [is] to those who take refuge in him.

en.L: Every word of God [is] refined; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] a shield to those who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Every word God speaks is proven true; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a shield to all who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Everything God says is true and pure. \q He protects everyone who goes to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety.

fr.L: Toute parole de Dieu [est] éprouvée ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [est] un bouclier pour ceux qui se réfugient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Toute parole que Dieu dit a fait ses preuves ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est un bouclier pour tous ceux qui se réfugient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Tout ce que Dieu dit est vrai et pur. \q Il protège tous ceux qui viennent se mettre à l’abri auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kila neno la Mungu [limesafishwa]; \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [ni] ngao kwa wale wanaokimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Kila neno asemalo Mungu limethibitika kuwa kweli; \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni ngao kwa wote wanaokimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Kila asemalo Mungu ni kweli na safi. \q Yeye humlinda kila mtu anayekimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ili awe salama.

decisions.choice: God: Eloah
decisions.reason: The name here is Eloah, the form used often in Job, not the LORD's personal name.

decisions.choice: refined: tested like metal in a furnace, without flaw
decisions.reason: The word (tsaruph) is used of silver refined of dross. The verse is nearly the same as Psalm 18:31 and 2 Samuel 22:31. What humans cannot reach (verses 2–4) God gives in his word.

source.text: אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you are proved a liar.

en.L: Do not add to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words, \q or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rebuke you and you will be proved a liar.
en.B: Do not add anything to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words, \q or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will correct you and show you to be a liar.
en.R: Do not add your own ideas to what God says. \q If you do, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will correct you and show that you are lying.

fr.L: N’ajoute rien à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles, \q de peur qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne te reprenne et que tu ne sois trouvé menteur.
fr.B: N’ajoute rien à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles, \q sinon {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te corrigera et montrera que tu es un menteur.
fr.R: N’ajoute pas tes propres idées à ce que Dieu dit. \q Sinon, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te corrigera et montrera que tu mens.

sw.L: Usiongeze kwa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q asije akakukemea, nawe ukaonekana mwongo.
sw.B: Usiongeze chochote kwa maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q la sivyo atakurekebisha na kukuonyesha kuwa mwongo.
sw.R: Usiongeze mawazo yako mwenyewe kwa yale anayosema Mungu. \q Ukifanya hivyo, atakurekebisha na kuonyesha kwamba unasema uongo.

decisions.choice: do not add to his words: as in Deuteronomy 4:2
decisions.reason: Compare Deuteronomy 4:2; 12:32; Revelation 22:18.

source.text: שְׁ֭תַּיִם שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ אַל־תִּמְנַ֥ע מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי בְּטֶ֣רֶם אָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: Two [things] I ask from you; do not withhold [them] from me before I die:

en.L: Two [things] I ask of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q do not withhold [them] from me before I die:
en.B: I ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for two things; \q grant them to me before I die:
en.R: God, I ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for two things. \q Please give them to me while I am still alive:

fr.L: Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demande deux [choses] ; \q ne [me les] refuse pas avant que je meure :
fr.B: Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demande deux choses ; \q accorde-les-moi avant que je meure :
fr.R: Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demande deux choses. \q Donne-les-moi, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, pendant que je suis encore en vie :

sw.L: Mambo mawili ninaomba {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}; \q usininyime kabla sijafa:
sw.B: Ninakuomba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} mambo mawili; \q nijalie kabla sijafa:
sw.R: Mungu, ninakuomba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} mambo mawili. \q Tafadhali nipe ningali hai:

decisions.choice: you: God, to whom Agur prays
decisions.reason: The only prayer in Proverbs. The two requests follow in verse 8: keep me from falsehood, and give me neither poverty nor riches.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed, so that it is clear this is a prayer.

decisions.choice: Agur speaks to God with "tu" ("je te demande"), with the deity-pronoun setting on "te"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for prayer: French addresses God with "tu". The setting on "te" mirrors the English "you|You".

source.text: שָׁ֤וְא׀וּֽדְבַר־כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־תִּֽתֶּן־לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Emptiness and a word of falsehood put far from me; poverty and riches do not give to me; let me eat the food of my portion,

en.L: Put emptiness and a word of falsehood far from me; \q do not give me poverty or riches; \q let me eat the bread of my portion,
en.B: Keep falsehood and lies far away from me; \q give me neither poverty nor wealth, \q but feed me with the bread I need each day,
en.R: Keep me from lying and from things that are false. \q Do not make me poor, and do not make me rich. \q Just give me the food I need each day.

fr.L: Éloigne de moi la fausseté et la parole de mensonge ; \q ne me donne ni pauvreté ni richesse ; \q fais-moi manger le pain de ma part,
fr.B: Tiens loin de moi la fausseté et les mensonges ; \q ne me donne ni la pauvreté ni la richesse, \q mais nourris-moi du pain qu’il me faut chaque jour,
fr.R: Garde-moi de mentir et de ce qui est faux. \q Ne me rends pas pauvre, et ne me rends pas riche. \q Donne-moi seulement la nourriture dont j’ai besoin chaque jour.

sw.L: Uweke mbali nami ubatili na neno la uongo; \q usinipe umaskini wala utajiri; \q unilishe mkate wa fungu langu,
sw.B: Uweke mbali nami udanganyifu na uongo; \q usinipe umaskini wala mali, \q bali unilishe mkate ninaohitaji kila siku,
sw.R: Unizuie nisiseme uongo wala nisifuate mambo ya uongo. \q Usinifanye maskini, wala usinifanye tajiri. \q Unipe tu chakula ninachohitaji kila siku.

decisions.choice: emptiness: what is false and worthless
decisions.reason: The word (shav) is used of empty, deceptive things, including false worship (Exodus 20:7; Psalm 31:7).

decisions.choice: the bread of my portion: the food allotted to me day by day
decisions.reason: The word (hoq) is a fixed share, as in 31:15. Compare the daily manna (Exodus 16:4) and the prayer for daily bread (Matthew 6:11).

source.text: פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע׀וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: lest I be full and deny and say, "Who [is] YHWH?" and lest I become poor and steal and lay hold of the name of my God.

en.L: lest I be full and deny [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] and say, \q "Who [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" \q or lest I become poor and steal, \q and profane the name of my God.
en.B: so that I do not have too much and disown {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, asking, \q "Who is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" \q or have too little and steal, \q and so bring disgrace on my God's name.
en.R: If I have too much, I might forget {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and say, "Who is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" \q If I am too poor, I might steal and bring shame on my God's name.

fr.L: de peur que, rassasié, je ne [{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}] renie et ne dise : \q « Qui [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » \q ou que, devenu pauvre, je ne vole, \q et ne profane le nom de mon Dieu.
fr.B: pour que je n’aie pas trop et ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} renie en disant : \q « Qui est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » \q ni trop peu et que je ne vole, \q couvrant ainsi de honte le nom de mon Dieu.
fr.R: Si j’ai trop, je risque de {{deity_pronoun:t|T}}oublier et de dire : « Qui est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » \q Si je suis trop pauvre, je risque de voler et de couvrir de honte le nom de mon Dieu.

sw.L: nisije nikashiba nikakukana na kusema, \q "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni] nani?" \q au nisije nikawa maskini nikaiba, \q nikalitia unajisi jina la Mungu wangu.
sw.B: nisije nikawa na vingi mno nikakukana, nikisema, \q "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni nani?" \q au nikawa na kidogo mno nikaiba, \q na hivyo nikaliletea aibu jina la Mungu wangu.
sw.R: Nikiwa na vingi mno, huenda nikakusahau na kusema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni nani?" \q Nikiwa maskini mno, huenda nikaiba na kuliletea aibu jina la Mungu wangu.

decisions.choice: full and deny: forgetting God in plenty
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 8:10–14 warns that when Israel has eaten its fill it may forget the LORD. Compare Pharaoh's "Who is the LORD?" (Exodus 5:2).

decisions.choice: lay hold of the name of my God: bring it into disrepute
decisions.reason: The verb (taphas) is to seize; to handle God's name is to profane it, perhaps by swearing falsely when accused of theft (Leviticus 6:2–3).

decisions.choice: deny you
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Since Agur is praying, the one he would deny is God himself.

source.text: אַל־תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד אֶל־אֲדֹנָ֑יו פֶּֽן־יְקַלֶּלְךָ֥ וְאָשָֽׁמְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not slander a slave to his master, lest he curse you and you are held guilty.

en.L: Do not slander a servant to his master, \q lest he curse you and you be held guilty.
en.B: Do not speak against a servant to his master, \q or the servant will call down a curse on you, and you will be found guilty.
en.R: Do not tell lies about a servant to his boss. \q The servant might ask God to punish you, and you will be guilty.

fr.L: Ne calomnie pas un esclave auprès de son maître, \q de peur qu’il ne te maudisse et que tu ne sois tenu pour coupable.
fr.B: Ne parle pas contre un serviteur auprès de son maître, \q sinon le serviteur appellera sur toi une malédiction, et tu seras reconnu coupable.
fr.R: Ne dis pas de mensonges sur un serviteur à son patron. \q Le serviteur pourrait demander à Dieu de te punir, et tu serais coupable.

sw.L: Usimchongee mtumwa kwa bwana wake, \q asije akakulaani nawe ukahesabiwa kuwa na hatia.
sw.B: Usimseme vibaya mtumishi kwa bwana wake, \q la sivyo mtumishi huyo atakulaani, nawe utapatikana na hatia.
sw.R: Usiseme uongo juu ya mtumishi kwa bosi wake. \q Mtumishi huyo anaweza kumwomba Mungu akuadhibu, nawe utakuwa na hatia.

decisions.choice: his master, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written form and the scribes' reading differ in spelling; both mean "his master."

decisions.choice: he will curse you: the slandered servant
decisions.reason: A servant has no other defense than to call on God against the slanderer, and the curse is deserved (contrast 26:2).

source.text: דּ֭וֹר אָבִ֣יו יְקַלֵּ֑ל וְאֶת־אִ֝מּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְבָרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: A generation curses its father, and its mother it does not bless.

en.L: [There is] a generation [that] curses its father \q and does not bless its mother.
en.B: There are people who curse their fathers \q and never speak well of their mothers.
en.R: Some people curse their fathers. \q They have nothing good to say about their mothers.

fr.L: [Il y a] une génération [qui] maudit son père \q et ne bénit pas sa mère.
fr.B: Il y a des gens qui maudissent leur père \q et ne disent jamais de bien de leur mère.
fr.R: Certains maudissent leur père. \q Ils n’ont rien de bon à dire sur leur mère.

sw.L: [Kuna] kizazi [kinachomlaani] baba yake \q wala hakimbariki mama yake.
sw.B: Kuna watu wanaowalaani baba zao \q na kamwe hawawasemi mama zao vizuri.
sw.R: Watu wengine huwalaani baba zao. \q Hawana neno jema la kusema juu ya mama zao.

decisions.choice: a generation: a kind of people
decisions.reason: The word (dor) can mean a class of people with a common character (Psalm 24:6). Verses 11–14 describe four marks of such people: contempt for parents, self-righteousness, pride, and cruelty.

decisions.choice: curses its father
decisions.reason: Cursing a parent was a capital crime under the law (Exodus 21:17). Compare 20:20; 30:17.

source.text: דּ֭וֹר טָה֣וֹר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וּ֝מִצֹּאָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רֻחָֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: A generation pure in its eyes, but from its filth it has not been washed.

en.L: [There is] a generation [that is] pure in its own eyes, \q yet it has not been washed from its filth.
en.B: There are people who think they are clean, \q yet their filth has never been washed away.
en.R: Some people think they are pure. \q But they are still dirty with sin.

fr.L: [Il y a] une génération [qui est] pure à ses propres yeux, \q et pourtant elle n’a pas été lavée de sa souillure.
fr.B: Il y a des gens qui se croient purs, \q et pourtant leur saleté n’a jamais été lavée.
fr.R: Certains se croient purs. \q Mais ils sont encore sales de leur péché.

sw.L: [Kuna] kizazi [kilicho] safi machoni pake chenyewe, \q lakini hakijaoshwa uchafu wake.
sw.B: Kuna watu wanaodhani ni safi, \q lakini uchafu wao haujaoshwa kamwe.
sw.R: Watu wengine hudhani ni safi. \q Lakini bado ni wachafu kwa dhambi.

decisions.choice: its filth: excrement
decisions.reason: The word (tso) is a strong, coarse word for filth (Isaiah 4:4; 28:8).

source.text: דּ֭וֹר מָה־רָמ֣וּ עֵינָ֑יו וְ֝עַפְעַפָּ֗יו יִנָּשֵֽׂאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: A generation, how lofty [are] its eyes, and its eyelids are lifted up!

en.L: [There is] a generation, how lofty [are] its eyes, \q and its eyelids are lifted up!
en.B: There are people whose eyes are so haughty, \q whose glances are full of scorn!
en.R: Some people are so proud! \q They look down on everyone.

fr.L: [Il y a] une génération, que ses yeux sont hautains, \q et ses paupières sont relevées !
fr.B: Il y a des gens qui ont le regard si hautain, \q et des yeux pleins de mépris !
fr.R: Certains sont si orgueilleux ! \q Ils regardent tout le monde de haut.

sw.L: [Kuna] kizazi, jinsi macho yake [yalivyo] ya kiburi, \q na kope zake zimeinuliwa juu!
sw.B: Kuna watu ambao macho yao yana kiburi kingi mno, \q ambao mitazamo yao imejaa dharau!
sw.R: Watu wengine wana kiburi kingi mno! \q Huwadharau watu wote.

decisions.choice: lofty eyes: pride
decisions.reason: As in 6:17 and 21:4.

source.text: דּ֤וֹר׀חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ וּֽמַאֲכָל֪וֹת מְֽתַלְּעֹ֫תָ֥יולֶאֱכֹ֣ל עֲנִיִּ֣ים מֵאֶ֑רֶץ וְ֝אֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים מֵאָדָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: A generation [whose] teeth [are] swords and [whose] jaws [are] knives, to devour [the] afflicted from [the] earth and [the] needy from among humankind.

en.L: [There is] a generation [whose] teeth [are] swords and [whose] jaws [are] knives, \q to devour [the] afflicted from [the] earth \q and [the] needy from among humankind.
en.B: There are people whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are set with knives, \q to devour the afflicted off the earth \q and the needy from the human race.
en.R: Some people are like wild animals with teeth as sharp as swords and knives. \q They destroy poor people and take everything they have.

fr.L: [Il y a] une génération [dont] les dents [sont] des épées et [dont] les mâchoires [sont] des couteaux, \q pour dévorer les humbles de la terre \q et les indigents parmi les humains.
fr.B: Il y a des gens dont les dents sont des épées et les mâchoires des couteaux, \q pour dévorer les humbles et les ôter de la terre, \q et les indigents du milieu des humains.
fr.R: Certains sont comme des bêtes sauvages aux dents aussi tranchantes que des épées et des couteaux. \q Ils détruisent les pauvres et leur prennent tout ce qu’ils ont.

sw.L: [Kuna] kizazi [ambacho] meno yake [ni] panga na magego yake [ni] visu, \q kuwala wanyonge watoweke duniani \q na wahitaji [watoweke] miongoni mwa wanadamu.
sw.B: Kuna watu ambao meno yao ni panga na magego yao ni visu, \q ili kuwala wanyonge watoweke duniani \q na wahitaji watoweke katika jamii ya wanadamu.
sw.R: Watu wengine ni kama wanyama wa porini wenye meno makali kama panga na visu. \q Huwaangamiza maskini na kuwanyang'anya kila kitu walicho nacho.

decisions.choice: teeth like swords: ruthless greed
decisions.reason: The picture is of a beast devouring prey. The poor are eaten up by oppression (Psalm 14:4; Micah 3:2–3).

decisions.choice: "les humbles" and "les indigents" for the afflicted and the needy
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for these words; Readable says simply "les pauvres", as the English does.

source.text: לַֽעֲלוּקָ֨ה׀שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ הַ֤ב׀הַ֥ב שָׁל֣וֹשׁ הֵ֭נָּה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־אָ֥מְרוּ הֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: To a leech [are] two daughters: "Give! Give!" Three [things] they are not satisfied; four do not say, "Enough!":

en.L: [The] leech has two daughters, "Give!" [and] "Give!" Three [things] are never satisfied; \q four never say, "Enough!":
en.B: The leech has two daughters, both called "Give!" Three things can never be filled; \q four never say, "Enough!":
en.R: A leech has two daughters, and both are named "Give me!" \q There are three things, even four, that always want more and never say, "That is enough!":

fr.L: La sangsue a deux filles : « Donne ! » [et] « Donne ! » Trois [choses] ne sont jamais rassasiées ; \q quatre ne disent jamais : « Assez ! » :
fr.B: La sangsue a deux filles, qui s’appellent toutes deux « Donne ! ». Trois choses ne sont jamais remplies ; \q quatre ne disent jamais : « Assez ! » :
fr.R: Une sangsue a deux filles, et toutes deux s’appellent « Donne-moi ! ». \q Il y a trois choses, et même quatre, qui en veulent toujours plus et ne disent jamais : « Ça suffit ! » :

sw.L: Ruba ana binti wawili, "Nipe!" [na] "Nipe!" Kuna [vitu] vitatu visivyoshiba kamwe; \q vinne visivyosema kamwe, "Inatosha!":
sw.B: Ruba ana binti wawili, wote wanaitwa "Nipe!" Kuna vitu vitatu visivyoweza kujazwa kamwe; \q vinne visivyosema kamwe, "Inatosha!":
sw.R: Ruba ana binti wawili, na wote wawili wanaitwa "Nipe!" \q Kuna vitu vitatu, naam, vinne, vinavyotaka zaidi siku zote na kamwe havisemi, "Inatosha sasa!":

decisions.choice: leech: the bloodsucking worm
decisions.reason: The word (aluqah) appears only here. Its two "daughters" may be its two suckers, named for what they always ask.

decisions.choice: three ... four: a numerical saying
decisions.reason: The pattern "three, even four" builds to the last item, which is often the point (Amos 1:3; Job 5:19). Verses 15–31 contain several such sayings.

source.text: שְׁאוֹל֮ וְעֹ֪צֶ֫ר רָ֥חַם אֶ֭רֶץ לֹא־שָׂ֣בְעָה מַּ֑יִם וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לֹא־אָ֥מְרָה הֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Sheol, and [the] barrenness of a womb, a land [that] is not satisfied [with] water, and fire [that] does not say, "Enough!"

en.L: Sheol, and [the] barren womb, \q [the] land [that] is never satisfied [with] water, \q and fire [that] never says, "Enough!"
en.B: Sheol, the barren womb, \q land that never has its fill of water, \q and fire that never says, "Enough!"
en.R: The grave, a woman who longs for children but has none, \q dry ground that always needs more rain, \q and fire that keeps on burning.

fr.L: le Shéol, et le sein stérile, \q la terre [qui] n’est jamais rassasiée d’eau, \q et le feu [qui] ne dit jamais : « Assez ! »
fr.B: le séjour des morts, le sein stérile, \q la terre qui n’a jamais assez d’eau, \q et le feu qui ne dit jamais : « Assez ! »
fr.R: la tombe, une femme qui désire des enfants mais n’en a pas, \q la terre sèche qui a toujours besoin de plus de pluie, \q et le feu qui ne cesse de brûler.

sw.L: Kuzimu, na tumbo lisilozaa, \q nchi isiyoshiba maji kamwe, \q na moto usiosema kamwe, "Inatosha!"
sw.B: Kuzimu, tumbo lisilozaa, \q ardhi isiyotosheka kamwe na maji, \q na moto usiosema kamwe, "Inatosha!"
sw.R: Kaburi, mwanamke anayetamani watoto lakini hana, \q ardhi kavu inayohitaji mvua zaidi siku zote, \q na moto unaoendelea kuwaka.

decisions.choice: Sheol: never full
decisions.reason: As in 27:20; compare Habakkuk 2:5.

decisions.choice: the barren womb: a childless woman's longing
decisions.reason: Compare Rachel's cry, "Give me children" (Genesis 30:1).

source.text: עַ֤יִן׀תִּֽלְעַ֣ג לְאָב֮ וְתָב֪וּז לִֽיקֲּהַ֫ת־אֵ֥ם יִקְּר֥וּהָ עֹרְבֵי־נַ֑חַל וְֽיֹאכְל֥וּהָ בְנֵי־נָֽשֶׁר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: An eye [that] mocks a father and despises obedience to a mother, the ravens of the valley will peck it out, and the young of the vulture will eat it.

en.L: [The] eye [that] mocks a father and despises obeying a mother, \q the ravens of the valley will peck it out, \q and [the] young vultures will eat it.
en.B: The eye that sneers at a father and scorns to obey a mother \q will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley \q and eaten by young vultures.
en.R: If you make fun of your father and refuse to obey your mother, \q you will die in disgrace, \q and the birds will eat your body.

fr.L: L’œil [qui] se moque d’un père et méprise l’obéissance à une mère, \q les corbeaux du torrent le crèveront, \q et les petits du vautour le mangeront.
fr.B: L’œil qui se moque d’un père et refuse avec mépris d’obéir à une mère \q sera arraché par les corbeaux de la vallée \q et dévoré par les petits des vautours.
fr.R: Si tu te moques de ton père et refuses d’obéir à ta mère, \q tu mourras dans la honte, \q et les oiseaux mangeront ton corps.

sw.L: Jicho linalomdhihaki baba na kudharau kumtii mama, \q kunguru wa bondeni watalidonoa, \q na makinda ya tai watalila.
sw.B: Jicho linalomdharau baba na kukataa kumtii mama \q litadonolewa na kunguru wa bondeni \q na kuliwa na makinda ya tai.
sw.R: Ukimdhihaki baba yako na kukataa kumtii mama yako, \q utakufa kwa aibu, \q na ndege watakula mwili wako.

decisions.choice: obedience: or perhaps the old age of a mother
alternatives: the old age of a mother
decisions.reason: The word (yiqqahat) is rare (Genesis 49:10). It most likely means obedience; some read it as a mother's gray hair or old age.

decisions.choice: eaten by birds: death without burial
decisions.reason: To lie unburied as food for birds was the worst disgrace (Deuteronomy 28:26; 1 Kings 14:11). The word (nesher) means both eagle and vulture.

decisions.choice: you will die in disgrace, and the birds will eat your body
alternatives: the ravens will peck out your eye
decisions.reason: Readable states the meaning of the picture: an unburied, shameful death.

source.text: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה נִפְלְא֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְדַעְתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Three [things] are too wonderful for me, and four I do not know:

en.L: Three [things] are too wonderful for me, \q and four I do not understand:
en.B: There are three things that amaze me, \q four that are beyond my understanding:
en.R: There are three things, even four, that are too amazing for me to understand:

fr.L: Trois [choses] sont trop merveilleuses pour moi, \q et quatre que je ne comprends pas :
fr.B: Il y a trois choses qui m’étonnent, \q quatre qui dépassent mon intelligence :
fr.R: Il y a trois choses, et même quatre, trop étonnantes pour que je les comprenne :

sw.L: [Kuna mambo] matatu yaliyo ya ajabu mno kwangu, \q na manne nisiyoyaelewa:
sw.B: Kuna mambo matatu yanayonishangaza, \q manne yaliyo juu ya ufahamu wangu:
sw.R: Kuna mambo matatu, naam, manne, yanayonishangaza mno nisiweze kuyaelewa:

decisions.choice: and four, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written form and the scribes' reading differ only in the form of the number; the sense is the same.

source.text: דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַנֶּ֨שֶׁר׀בַּשָּׁמַיִם֮ דֶּ֥רֶךְ נָחָ֗שׁ עֲלֵ֫י צ֥וּר דֶּֽרֶךְ־אֳנִיָּ֥ה בְלֶב־יָ֑ם וְדֶ֖רֶךְ גֶּ֣בֶר בְּעַלְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The way of the eagle in the heavens, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.

en.L: The way of the eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, \q the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, \q and the way of a man with a young woman.
en.B: An eagle making its way through the sky, a snake gliding over a rock, \q a ship finding its way across the open sea, \q and the way a man and a young woman come together.
en.R: How an eagle flies in the sky, how a snake moves across a rock, \q how a ship finds its way on the ocean, \q and how a man and a young woman fall in love.

fr.L: le chemin de l’aigle dans le ciel, le chemin du serpent sur le rocher, \q le chemin du navire au cœur de la mer, \q et le chemin de l’homme avec la jeune femme.
fr.B: l’aigle qui fait son chemin dans le ciel, le serpent qui glisse sur le rocher, \q le navire qui trouve sa route en pleine mer, \q et la manière dont un homme et une jeune femme s’unissent.
fr.R: comment l’aigle vole dans le ciel, comment le serpent avance sur un rocher, \q comment le bateau trouve son chemin sur l’océan, \q et comment un homme et une jeune femme tombent amoureux.

sw.L: Njia ya tai angani, njia ya nyoka juu ya mwamba, \q njia ya meli katikati ya bahari, \q na njia ya mwanamume pamoja na msichana.
sw.B: Tai anavyopita angani, nyoka anavyoteleza juu ya mwamba, \q meli inavyopata njia yake katika bahari kuu, \q na jinsi mwanamume na msichana wanavyoungana.
sw.R: Jinsi tai anavyoruka angani, jinsi nyoka anavyotambaa juu ya mwamba, \q jinsi meli inavyopata njia baharini, \q na jinsi mwanamume na msichana wanavyopendana.

decisions.choice: the way: a path that leaves no trace, a mystery of movement
decisions.reason: Each "way" is a wonder: how the eagle, the snake and the ship move with no road or track. The last, the way of a man with a young woman, is the climax: the mystery of love between them.

decisions.choice: a young woman: a woman of marriageable age
decisions.reason: The word (almah) is a young woman (Genesis 24:43; Isaiah 7:14).

source.text: כֵּ֤ן׀דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה מְנָ֫אָ֥פֶת אָ֭כְלָה וּמָ֣חֲתָה פִ֑יהָ וְ֝אָמְרָ֗ה לֹֽא־פָעַ֥לְתִּי אָֽוֶן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Thus [is] the way of an adulterous woman: she eats and wipes her mouth and says, "I have not done wickedness."

en.L: Thus [is] the way of an adulterous woman: \q she eats and wipes her mouth \q and says, "I have done no wrong."
en.B: This is how an adulteress behaves: \q she eats, wipes her mouth, \q and says, "I did no wrong."
en.R: A woman who cheats on her husband acts as if nothing happened. \q It is like eating a meal and wiping her mouth. \q Then she says, "I did nothing wrong."

fr.L: Tel [est] le chemin de la femme adultère : \q elle mange et s’essuie la bouche, \q et dit : « Je n’ai pas fait de mal. »
fr.B: Voici comment agit la femme adultère : \q elle mange, s’essuie la bouche, \q et dit : « Je n’ai rien fait de mal. »
fr.R: Une femme qui trompe son mari fait comme si rien ne s’était passé. \q C’est comme si elle prenait un repas et s’essuyait la bouche. \q Puis elle dit : « Je n’ai rien fait de mal. »

sw.L: Ndivyo [ilivyo] njia ya mwanamke mzinzi: \q hula na kupangusa kinywa chake \q na kusema, "Sijatenda uovu."
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo mwanamke mzinzi anavyotenda: \q hula, hupangusa kinywa chake, \q na kusema, "Sikufanya kosa lolote."
sw.R: Mwanamke anayemsaliti mumewe hujifanya kana kwamba hakuna kilichotokea. \q Ni kama kula chakula na kupangusa kinywa chake. \q Kisha husema, "Sikufanya kosa lolote."

decisions.choice: she eats and wipes her mouth: sins and leaves no trace
decisions.reason: Eating is a picture of the sexual act (9:17). Like the ways in verse 19, her way leaves no trace, and she feels no guilt.

source.text: תַּ֣חַת שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ רָ֣גְזָה אֶ֑רֶץ וְתַ֥חַת אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל שְׂאֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: Under three [things] the earth trembles, and under four it is not able to bear up:

en.L: Under three [things] the earth trembles, \q and under four it cannot bear up:
en.B: The earth shakes under three things; \q there are four it cannot endure:
en.R: There are three things, even four, that the world cannot stand:

fr.L: Sous trois [choses] la terre tremble, \q et sous quatre elle ne peut tenir :
fr.B: La terre tremble sous trois choses ; \q il y en a quatre qu’elle ne peut supporter :
fr.R: Il y a trois choses, et même quatre, que le monde ne peut pas supporter :

sw.L: Chini ya [mambo] matatu dunia hutetemeka, \q na chini ya manne haiwezi kustahimili:
sw.B: Dunia hutikisika chini ya mambo matatu; \q kuna manne isiyoweza kuyavumilia:
sw.R: Kuna mambo matatu, naam, manne, ambayo dunia haiwezi kuyavumilia:

decisions.choice: the earth trembles: the social order is upset
decisions.reason: Each of the four cases in verses 22–23 is a person suddenly raised to a place they are not fit for.

source.text: תַּֽחַת־עֶ֭בֶד כִּ֣י יִמְל֑וֹךְ וְ֝נָבָ֗ל כִּ֣י יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: under a slave when he becomes king, and a fool when he is filled with food,

en.L: under a slave when he becomes king, \q and a fool when he is filled with food,

sw.R: mtumishi anayekuwa mfalme, \q mpumbavu aliye na chakula tele,

decisions.choice: a fool (nabal): a godless, boorish person
decisions.reason: The word is the name of the churlish Nabal (1 Samuel 25:25). Prosperity makes such a person unbearable (compare 19:10).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: תַּ֣חַת שְׂ֭נוּאָה כִּ֣י תִבָּעֵ֑ל וְ֝שִׁפְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־תִירַ֥שׁ גְּבִרְתָּֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: under a hated [woman] when she is married, and a maidservant when she displaces her mistress.

en.L: under a hated [woman] when she gets married, \q and a maidservant when she displaces her mistress.
en.B: an unloved woman who finally gets a husband, \q and a servant girl who takes her mistress's place.
en.R: a woman no one loves who gets married, \q and a servant who takes the place of the woman she worked for.

fr.L: sous la [femme] haïe quand elle se marie, \q et la servante quand elle supplante sa maîtresse.
fr.B: la femme mal aimée qui trouve enfin un mari, \q et la servante qui prend la place de sa maîtresse.
fr.R: une femme que personne n’aime et qui se marie, \q et une servante qui prend la place de la femme pour qui elle travaillait.

sw.L: chini ya [mwanamke] anayechukiwa anapoolewa, \q na mjakazi anapochukua nafasi ya bibi yake.
sw.B: mwanamke asiyependwa anayepata mume hatimaye, \q na mjakazi anayechukua nafasi ya bibi yake.
sw.R: mwanamke asiyependwa na mtu yeyote anayeolewa, \q na mtumishi anayechukua nafasi ya mwanamke aliyemfanyia kazi.

decisions.choice: a maidservant displacing her mistress
decisions.reason: The case of Hagar and Sarah shows the strife it caused (Genesis 16:4–5). The verb (yarash) is to take possession, perhaps by becoming the husband's favored wife or heir.

source.text: אַרְבָּ֣עָה הֵ֭ם קְטַנֵּי־אָ֑רֶץ וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים מְחֻכָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Four [things] are small [things] of [the] earth, but they are wise, made wise:

en.L: Four [things] on earth are small, \q but they are exceedingly wise:
en.B: On earth there are four small creatures \q that are wiser than the wise:
en.R: There are four small animals on earth that are very wise:

fr.L: Quatre [choses] sur la terre sont petites, \q mais elles sont plus sages que les sages :
fr.B: Sur la terre il y a quatre petites bêtes \q qui sont plus sages que les sages :
fr.R: Il y a sur la terre quatre petits animaux qui sont très sages :

sw.L: [Viko vitu] vinne duniani vilivyo vidogo, \q lakini vina hekima nyingi mno:
sw.B: Duniani kuna viumbe vinne vidogo \q vilivyo na hekima kuliko wenye hekima:
sw.R: Kuna wanyama wanne wadogo duniani walio na hekima nyingi:

decisions.choice: wise, made wise: exceedingly wise
decisions.reason: The repetition of the root (hakham) is emphatic: they are wise beyond their size.

source.text: הַ֭נְּמָלִים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָ֑ז וַיָּכִ֖ינוּ בַקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: The ants [are] a people not strong, yet they prepare in summer their food;

en.L: The ants [are] a people not strong, \q yet they prepare their food in summer;
en.B: ants are a people without strength, \q yet they store up their food in summer;
en.R: Ants are not strong, \q but they gather food in the summer to eat later.

fr.L: les fourmis, peuple sans force, \q préparent pourtant leur nourriture en été ;
fr.B: les fourmis sont un peuple sans force, \q et pourtant elles font leurs provisions en été ;
fr.R: Les fourmis ne sont pas fortes, \q mais elles ramassent de la nourriture en été pour la manger plus tard.

sw.L: Chungu [ni] watu wasio na nguvu, \q hata hivyo hujiandalia chakula chao wakati wa kiangazi;
sw.B: chungu ni jamii isiyo na nguvu, \q hata hivyo huweka akiba ya chakula chao wakati wa kiangazi;
sw.R: Chungu hawana nguvu, \q lakini hukusanya chakula wakati wa kiangazi ili wale baadaye.

decisions.choice: the ants: foresight
decisions.reason: As in 6:6–8.

source.text: שְׁ֭פַנִּים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָצ֑וּם וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ בַסֶּ֣לַע בֵּיתָֽם׃

en.L: rock badgers [are] a people not mighty, \q yet they make their home in the rock;
en.B: rock badgers are a feeble folk, \q yet they set up house among the crags;
en.R: Rock badgers are weak, \q but they live safely among the rocks.

fr.L: les damans, peuple sans puissance, \q établissent pourtant leur demeure dans le rocher ;
fr.B: les damans sont un peuple faible, \q et pourtant ils font leur maison au milieu des rochers ;
fr.R: Les damans sont faibles, \q mais ils vivent en sécurité au milieu des rochers.

sw.L: wibari [ni] watu wasio na uwezo, \q hata hivyo hujifanyia makao yao miambani;
sw.B: wibari ni jamii dhaifu, \q hata hivyo hujenga makao yao katikati ya miamba;
sw.R: Wibari ni dhaifu, \q lakini huishi salama katikati ya miamba.

decisions.choice: rock badgers: the rock hyrax
decisions.reason: The hyrax (shaphan) is a small animal that lives in rocky places and hides in crevices (Psalm 104:18).

decisions.choice: "les damans" for the rock badgers
decisions.reason: The animal is the rock hyrax (meaning decision m1), which French calls "daman"; it is not a badger.

en.B: locusts have no king, \q yet they all march out in ordered ranks;
en.R: Locusts have no king, \q but they move forward together like an army.

fr.R: Les sauterelles n’ont pas de roi, \q mais elles avancent ensemble comme une armée.

decisions.choice: dividing: in divisions, in ranks
decisions.reason: The verb (hatsats) suggests dividing into companies, like an army (Joel 2:7–8).

en.B: a lizard can be caught in the hand, \q yet it lives in kings' palaces.
en.R: You can catch a lizard with your hands, \q but it lives in a king's palace.

sw.R: Unaweza kumkamata mjusi kwa mikono yako, \q lakini anaishi katika jumba la mfalme.

decisions.choice: lizard: probably a gecko
decisions.reason: The word (semamit) appears only here. It is most likely a gecko, which clings to walls and goes everywhere; older versions took it as a spider.

decisions.choice: you can grasp with hands
decisions.reason: The verb may be "you catch" or "she grasps": the gecko holds on with its feet. Either way, a small, weak creature lives where the great live.

decisions.reason: The four examples in verses 30–31 move with confidence and dignity.

decisions.reason: A poetic word for a lion.

records.literal_gloss: a girded of loins or a male goat, and a king [with] a band of soldiers with him.

en.L: a strutting rooster or a male goat, \q and a king [with] his army around him.
en.B: the strutting rooster, the he-goat, \q and a king at the head of his troops.
en.R: a proud rooster, a male goat, \q and a king leading his army.

fr.L: le coq qui se pavane ou le bouc, \q et le roi [avec] son armée autour de lui.
fr.B: le coq qui se pavane, le bouc, \q et le roi à la tête de ses troupes.
fr.R: un coq fier, un bouc, \q et un roi qui conduit son armée.

sw.B: jogoo anayetamba, beberu, \q na mfalme akiongoza majeshi yake.
sw.R: jogoo mwenye majivuno, beberu, \q na mfalme anayeongoza jeshi lake.

decisions.choice: girded of loins: probably a strutting rooster
decisions.reason: The phrase (zarzir motnayim) appears only here; literally something "girded at the waist." Ancient versions took it as a rooster; others suggest a greyhound or a warhorse.

decisions.choice: a band of soldiers with him
decisions.reason: The word (alqum) is unknown elsewhere. It is usually understood as "his army with him"; it may instead be read "no one rising against him."

source.text: אִם־נָבַ֥לְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א וְאִם־זַ֝מּ֗וֹתָ יָ֣ד לְפֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, and if you have planned [evil], hand to mouth!

en.L: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, \q or if you have plotted [evil], \q [put your] hand to [your] mouth!
en.B: If you have played the fool by putting yourself forward, \q or if you have been scheming, \q put your hand over your mouth!
en.R: If you have been foolish and acted proud, \q or if you have planned to do something wrong, stop and keep quiet!

fr.L: Si tu as été insensé en t’élevant, \q ou si tu as médité [le mal], \q [mets ta] main sur [ta] bouche !
fr.B: Si tu as fait l’insensé en te mettant en avant, \q ou si tu as comploté, \q mets ta main sur ta bouche !
fr.R: Si tu as été insensé et orgueilleux, \q ou si tu as projeté de faire quelque chose de mal, arrête-toi et tais-toi !

sw.L: Ikiwa umefanya upumbavu kwa kujikweza, \q au ikiwa umepanga [maovu], \q [weka] mkono kinywani!
sw.B: Ikiwa umefanya upumbavu kwa kujitanguliza, \q au ikiwa umekuwa ukipanga hila, \q weka mkono wako juu ya kinywa chako!
sw.R: Ikiwa umefanya upumbavu na kujivuna, \q au ikiwa umepanga kutenda jambo baya, acha na unyamaze!

decisions.choice: hand to mouth: be silent
decisions.reason: Covering the mouth is a gesture of silence and shame (Job 21:5; 40:4).

decisions.choice: planned: plotted evil
decisions.reason: The verb (zamam) usually means to devise evil (Psalm 37:12).

source.text: כִּ֤י מִ֪יץ חָלָ֡ב י֘וֹצִ֤יא חֶמְאָ֗ה וּֽמִיץ־אַ֭ף י֣וֹצִיא דָ֑ם וּמִ֥יץ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם י֣וֹצִיא רִֽיב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For squeezing of milk brings out curds, and squeezing of a nose brings out blood, and squeezing of anger brings out strife.

en.L: For [the] pressing of milk brings out curds, \q and [the] pressing of [the] nose brings out blood, \q and [the] pressing of anger brings out strife.
en.B: For as churning milk produces butter, \q and pressing the nose produces blood, \q so pressing anger produces a quarrel.
en.R: When you churn milk, you get butter. \q When you squeeze someone's nose, it bleeds. \q When you make someone angry, you get a fight.

fr.L: Car le pressage du lait fait sortir le beurre, \q et le pressage du nez fait sortir le sang, \q et le pressage de la colère fait sortir la querelle.
fr.B: Car comme en battant le lait on obtient du beurre, \q et en pressant le nez on fait couler le sang, \q ainsi en pressant la colère on provoque une dispute.
fr.R: Quand tu bats du lait, tu obtiens du beurre. \q Quand tu serres le nez de quelqu’un, il saigne. \q Quand tu mets quelqu’un en colère, tu provoques une dispute.

sw.L: Kwa maana kukamua maziwa hutoa siagi, \q na kukamua pua hutoa damu, \q na kukamua hasira hutoa ugomvi.
sw.B: Kwa maana kama kusukasuka maziwa kunavyotoa siagi, \q na kubana pua kunavyotoa damu, \q ndivyo kuchochea hasira kunavyoleta ugomvi.
sw.R: Ukisukasuka maziwa, unapata siagi. \q Ukimbana mtu pua, inatoka damu. \q Ukimkasirisha mtu, unapata ugomvi.

decisions.choice: nose ... anger: a play on words
decisions.reason: The word for nose (aph) is also the word for anger; its dual form (appayim) is used for anger here. To keep pressing a quarrel is like twisting a nose until it bleeds.

decisions.choice: curds: butter or thick sour milk
decisions.reason: The word (hemah) is the product of churning milk in a skin.

decisions.choice: "le nez ... la colère"
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "nose" and "anger" are the same word, *aph* (meaning decision m1). French cannot keep the pun; Literal repeats "le pressage" three times to keep the pattern of the saying.
